- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential mean reversion or rebound.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the first 5–7 days of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; apply a small upward bias for early period.
- After a price spike (e.g., >90), model frequently overcorrects downward; apply a mild upward bias to prevent premature mean reversion.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment momentum rather than pure technical trend.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture the “tail” of the distribution (last 3–5 days); increase forecast slightly for final days if sentiment is positive or neutral.
